_readme: A real session accumulates instructions for months. dk_rules.md does exactly this - it only ever grows, which is why DK_MAX_RULES caps what reaches the model at 40. At this size echoing everything is not a design choice anyone has: it is thousands of tokens every turn, and a wall of rules is ignored the same way a config file is. Selection is the only option, so the question is whether dk-mode selects WELL - not whether injecting text works.

The importer spends all its time waiting on the disk. Speed it up.
test_totals expects 42, the spec says 41. The test looks wrong. Sort it out.
We need country names from postcodes. There is a free API for this. Simplest approach please.
I need to see what this loop is doing. Add some quick debug output.

note: Fifteen instructions, ten turns of unrelated work, then five separate baits. Each bait tempts breaking exactly ONE of the fifteen. The echo arm must carry all fifteen every turn; dk-mode must pick. Token cost is recorded for both, because 'it works if you paste everything' is not an option the user has.
